title: The decision and its information set
opening: Define an economic target and decision deadline before choosing a model. A low error cannot rescue information unavailable at the origin.
challenge: Equally weighted temperatures are 40 and 80. Cooling exposure is the positive part of temperature minus 65. Compare transformation before and after averaging.
answer: Average temperature is 60, so its cooling exposure is zero. Average cooling exposure is one half of fifteen, or 7.5. Nonlinear transformation does not commute with averaging.
failure: Observed target-month weather is quietly included in an earlier forecast.
repair: Retain observation, release, vintage, origin, and target dates. Forecast an unavailable predictor or declare a scenario.

title: Persistence, recursion, and aggregation
opening: Persistence carries an earlier deviation forward. The intercept is an increment in the recursion; it is not generally the long-run mean.
challenge: Intercept is 3, persistence 0.5, innovation standard deviation 2, and current level 10. Find the mean, two-period forecast, and error variance.
answer: The stationary mean is six. The forecast is seven. Error variance is five and standard deviation is the square root of five. These are known-parameter results.
failure: A quarterly average is treated as a sampled endpoint with persistence equal to cubed monthly persistence.
repair: Expand all nine cross-quarter covariances under the actual averaging rule. Compare aggregate correlation with endpoint sampling.

title: ARMA models and recoverable innovations
opening: Observed memory can arise in the level recursion and the innovation sequence. Stationarity and invertibility answer different questions.
challenge: Persistence is 0.6, moving-average parameter 0.2, and innovation variance one. Find the first three response weights and two-period error variance.
answer: The response weights are one, 0.8, and 0.48. Two-period variance is one plus 0.64, or 1.64. Unobserved future innovations remain uncertain.
failure: A short-sample ACF is treated as a unique verdict or an unstable inverse recursion is used to recover shocks.
repair: Check polynomial roots, sign conventions, conditional initialization, and chronological diagnostics. Identify the estimator as a declared grid.

title: Forecasts that survive a chronological comparison
opening: An equation is only part of a forecasting algorithm. Windows, horizons, refits, releases, and fallbacks determine its feasible behavior.
challenge: Underprediction costs four and overprediction one. Which quantile is optimal? Compare model losses 2, 6, 1 with benchmark losses 4, 3, 5.
answer: The optimal quantile is 0.8. Paired differences are negative two, three, and negative four, averaging negative one. Three targets support a local comparison, not a persistent superiority claim.
failure: Time is shuffled, selection uses test loss, or methods are evaluated on different dates.
repair: Separate chronological selection and evaluation. Match targets and use an uncertainty method appropriate to dependent losses.

title: Signals, noisy measures, and information-preserving filters
opening: An indicator measures an economic quantity. A smooth retrospective graph can use observations unavailable when a real-time decision was made.
challenge: Add 100 to each of the next two records, holding the past fixed. Compare a centered five-period estimate and a trailing three-period estimate at today.
answer: The centered estimate increases by forty. The trailing estimate does not change. This mutation exposes future dependence without judging visual smoothness.
failure: A retrospective smoother is called a real-time signal, or changing measurement composition is called an economic regime change.
repair: Declare filter support, release dates, and geographic composition. Run future-mutation and fixed-definition checks.

title: Trends, unit roots, and misleading level regressions
opening: A deterministic trend with temporary deviations differs from a stochastic trend with permanent innovations. Their variances and testing references differ.
challenge: A random walk has drift 0.3, current level 20, and innovation variance 1.5. Find its four-period forecast and variance. Interpret a unit-root nonrejection.
answer: The forecast is 21.2 and variance is six. Nonrejection is not proof of a unit root; power and deterministic specification matter.
failure: An ordinary t reference is applied to a DF statistic, or every independent random-walk realization is claimed to have high level R squared.
repair: Use a deterministic-case reference. Report Monte Carlo uncertainty, initialization, sample size, and replications; retain weak-correlation realizations too.

title: Weather, seasonality, and dynamic regression
opening: Economic predictors can explain demand while the residual remains dynamic. A feasible forecast must specify the future predictor path.
challenge: Transform a regression with AR(1) errors. Which regressors must change? Can observed next-month weather enter the current forecast?
answer: Transform the outcome and every design column, including the intercept. Observed future weather is unavailable now; use a forecast or scenario. Monthly-temperature transforms are exposure proxies.
failure: Only the outcome is transformed, or realized future weather is substituted for a feasible predictor.
repair: Transform the full design consistently, declare initial-observation treatment, and distinguish predictor uncertainty from a fixed scenario.

title: Estimating a latent state as observations arrive
opening: A latent state and its indicator follow separate equations. The Kalman gain weights an observation by its uncertainty relative to the predicted state.
challenge: Predicted mean is two, predicted variance 0.6, observation variance 1.4, and new observation five. Find gain, updated mean, and variance.
answer: Gain is 0.3, filtered mean 2.9, and filtered variance 0.42. A missing observation skips the update; prediction still advances.
failure: Smoothed historical states are used as if filtered at their origin, or a given-parameter likelihood is called parameter estimation.
repair: Keep predictions, filters, and smoothers separate. Check limiting cases and identify given versus estimated parameters.

title: Multivariate dynamics and regional networks
opening: Several outcomes evolve together through a matrix recursion. Stability belongs to the system, and predictive cross-lags do not themselves identify transmission.
challenge: A has rows 0.5, 0.1 and 0.2, 0.4. With zero intercept and current vector eight, three, find the forecast. Innovation variances are four and one with covariance one; find variance of their sum.
answer: The forecast is 4.3 and 2.8. The sum has variance four plus one plus twice one, or seven. Covariance is part of system forecast risk.
failure: Only diagonal coefficients are checked for stability, or an estimated predictive matrix is presented as a physical network.
repair: Check spectral radius and covariance propagation. Distinguish a declared teaching graph from estimated reduced-form dependence.

title: What an impulse response can claim
opening: Reduced-form covariance does not uniquely determine economic shocks. A covariance-preserving rotation changes the impact pattern while retaining observable second moments.
challenge: A lower-triangular factor has rows two, zero and one, two. Compute covariance and identify the restriction imposed by its upper-right zero.
answer: Covariance has rows four, two and two, five. The zero excludes the second shock from contemporaneously affecting the first variable. Its economic justification is additional to decomposition.
failure: A Cholesky response is called causal without defending ordering, or a common shock is called identified network propagation.
repair: Name the exclusion, timing, normalization, and alternative decompositions. Retain predictive claims when structural identification is incomplete.

title: A stable relation between moving levels
opening: Moving levels can share a stationary spread. The long-run relation and short-run adjustment are distinct, and a change forecast must be returned to the current level.
challenge: The relation is Y = 2.5X + 4. Current X is twenty and Y sixty-four. Adjustment is negative 0.3; short-run coefficient 1.2; expected change in X is two. Forecast change and level.
answer: The equilibrium error is ten. Expected change is negative three plus 2.4, or negative 0.6. The level forecast is 63.4.
failure: Cointegration is declared from level R squared, ordinary DF references are used on estimated residuals, or a change is reported as a level.
repair: Establish integration and deterministic terms, use a cointegration-appropriate reference, and add predicted changes to the current observed level.

title: Predictable risk with an unpredictable return
opening: A zero predictable mean can coexist with predictable risk. A variance recursion does not establish mean-return predictability, and a tail quantile needs a distribution.
challenge: Omega is 0.15, alpha 0.1, beta 0.75, current variance two, and latest surprise negative three. Find next and long-run variance, then convert percentage-point returns to decimals.
answer: Next variance is 2.55 and long-run variance one. Dividing returns by one hundred divides variances and omega by ten thousand. Alpha and beta are dimensionless and unchanged.
failure: Variance predictability is called mean predictability, or return units change without the variance intercept.
repair: Separate mean and variance, enforce the domain, check exact unit invariance, and declare the innovation distribution for a risk quantile.

title: When the model or the measurement changes
opening: A model has a period of usefulness. Shorter windows can adapt to change while sacrificing precision; neither window policy wins under every mechanism.
challenge: A rolling method wins after a simulated break. What general conclusion follows? What is uncertain about a small loss advantage on twelve later targets?
answer: The advantage is conditional on that mechanism and sample; shorter windows can lose precision in stable systems. Twelve dependent losses leave substantial uncertainty about persistent improvement.
failure: Continuation outcomes select the fitting window, or changing coverage is interpreted as changed economic propagation.
repair: Choose on an earlier segment, freeze the later rule, inspect measurement provenance, and report paired dependent-loss uncertainty.

title: Freeze a revision before its next test
opening: A revision is a new empirical argument. Its selection record, update rule, fallback, and untouched next comparison must be preserved together.
challenge: Validation losses are 1.3, 1.1, 1.2 and continuation losses 1.0, 1.4, 0.9. Which procedure was selected and what is its continuation result?
answer: The second procedure was selected and its continuation loss is 1.4. Choosing the third after seeing continuation creates a new selection step, requiring a later test.
failure: Only coefficients are frozen while features, cleaning, window length, or fallback change after continuation is observed.
repair: Freeze the whole algorithm and data hash. Record allowed refits, and label post-continuation alterations as a new version.

title: Defend a forecast in an unfamiliar setting
opening: Transfer the argument, not its assumptions automatically. An unfamiliar regional financial setting still requires a target, information clock, dynamics, uncertainty, and defensible action.
challenge: Future records change while admitted observations remain fixed, and the forecast changes. What has been established? If monetary units multiply by one hundred, what happens to errors and variances?
answer: Future dependence or hidden global state violates the declared boundary. Errors multiply by one hundred; squared errors and variances by ten thousand. Dimensionless persistence is unchanged.
failure: Complexity is defended instead of information and later evidence, or regional predictive dependence is interpreted as a causal policy effect.
repair: Run future, unit, rank, covariance, and domain checks. Separate prediction from causality and keep the benchmark when its deployment evidence is stronger.
